simulator.challenger_cards.quoted_text: A player becomes the Challenger if, at the start of the battle round, they have fewer victory points than their opponent, and the difference between their victory point totals is 6 or more. While a player has the Challenger status, at the start of their Command phase they draw one Challenger card. For each Challenger card, you can complete the Mission, or you can use the card as a Stratagem - you cannot do both. (Chapter Approved 2025-26, Wahapedia rendering.) The Determine Victor victory-point-source table caps Challenger cards at a maximum of 12 victory points, with primary (max 50) + secondary (max 40) + challenger (max 12) combined capped at 90. There are 9 Challenger cards in the deck and each is worth 3 victory points if completed (Flipside Gaming, Goonhammer). COMPETITIVE EXCLUSION (decisive for this project): the Chapter Approved Tournament Companion - the matched-play/tournament ruleset the May 2026 Warp Friends aggregate is drawn from - explicitly states: 'This document does not use the full contents of your Chapter Approved Mission Deck ... we have not included the Asymmetric War cards, the Twist cards or the Challenger cards.' Challenger cards are therefore NOT in play in the competitive tournament games this simulator calibrates against.
simulator.challenger_cards.trigger: at the start of a battle round (rounds 2-5 in this simulator, since primary opens in round 2), the side whose victory-point total trails the opponent's by 6 or more draws ONE extra Challenger scoring card for that round. Even-handed: whichever side is trailing draws, by the identical rule, with no per-faction branch. The gap is read by default from the uncapped running totals (`_a_vp`/`_b_vp`); SWEG_CHALLENGER_GAP_CAPPED (default-off, held) reads the capped standing (`_capped_vp_pair`) instead, which is the more faithful reading of a capped-as-scored victory point but screened metric-negative (N=40 vs sc22a gated +0.11; Astra Militarum -1.91, Adeptus Astartes -1.77).
simulator.challenger_cards.effect: the trailing side draws ONE extra scoring card (an existing Tactical / take-and-hold objective, selected deterministically by a zlib.crc32 over both rosters' sorted unit-name multisets + round, consuming NO global RNG) and scores it end-of-round through the SAME achievement machinery the Tactical secondary deck uses (`Battle._score_one_card`); an army that cannot physically achieve the drawn objective scores 0 from it. The lifetime Challenger contribution per side is capped at 12 victory points (`_CHALLENGER_LIFETIME_CAP`), and Challenger victory points form a THIRD track peeled out of `_capped_vp_pair` / `_decide_winner`, subject to neither the primary-50 nor the secondary-40 cap. Implemented in `Battle._decide_challenger_draw` (round-start eligibility + deterministic draw, `code/simulator.py`) and `Battle._score_challenger_card` (end-of-round achievement scoring), called unconditionally in the `Battle.run` round loop with the gate check inside. APPROXIMATION: the real card is a fixed 3 victory points on a mission-or-stratagem choice; this models it as a variable-value Tactical-achievement draw capped at 12 lifetime, so the shape (trailing side gets a bounded catch-up avenue that fragile armies cannot bank) is faithful but the per-card magnitude is a proxy.
simulator.challenger_cards.note: Env-gated SWEG_CHALLENGER_CARDS. CURRENT STATE (reconciled 2026-07-04): the gate was flipped to default-ON at wave 252 (commit bc9159d, 'adopt ... Challenger catch-up cards (default-on)') and remains default-on in the standing sc53a anchor - the mechanic IS modelled and firing in production, contradicting the stale hardcoded 'NOT MODELLED' text in scripts/diag_signatures.py #8 and DECISION_LEDGER's 2026-07-04 'NOT MODELLED AT ALL' line, both of which predate/ignore the wave-252 build. OFF (`SWEG_CHALLENGER_CARDS=0`) is byte-identical (no draw, no victory points, no RNG). FIDELITY CAVEAT / RECOMMENDATION: because the competitive Tournament Companion excludes Challenger cards (quoted above), a competitively-calibrated simulator should arguably run this default-OFF; the wave-252 metric gain is a win-rate-spread compression from an out-of-reference catch-up dial, which trips the EVAL_PROTOCOL rule-9 guardrail ('no rate dial without an external real-meta reference'). Sources: Wahapedia Chapter Approved 2025-26 (URL above); warhammer-community.com Chapter Approved 2025-26 announcement (https://www.warhammer-community.com/en-gb/articles/ykj6czq0/chapter-approved-2025-asymmetric-missions-and-catch-up-mechanics-come-to-warhammer-40000/); Flipside Gaming 'Gambits, Secrets, and Challengers' (https://flipsidegaming.com/blogs/warhammer/warhammer-40k-gambits-secrets-and-challengers-catching-up-in-10th-edition); Chapter Approved Tournament Companion (https://assets.warhammer-community.com/eng_4-xglmycxyvf.pdf); docs/REAL_META_SIGNATURES.md lines 24-30.
